title: Lee Resolution Timeline
learningObjectives: Order Lee Resolution milestones from the 1775 Congress meeting through the 1777 confederation plan.
Identify the three parts of the Lee Resolution: independence, foreign alliances, and confederation.
Describe Congressional voting, including New York's delayed support on July 9, 1776.

evidence.quote: "that these united colonies are and of right ought to be free and independent states,"

explanations.text: The resolution proposed that the united colonies become free and independent states.

evidence.quote: one to draft a declaration of independence
a second to draw up a plan "for forming foreign alliances,"

explanations.text: Congress created three committees to draft independence, plan foreign alliances, and prepare confederation.

evidence.quote: the affirmative votes of 12 colonies are listed at the right
the plan of confederation was delayed until November of 1777

explanations.text: Twelve colonies voted affirmative while New York waited, and treaty and confederation plans came months later.

evidence.quote: Its second meeting convened in Philadelphia in 1775.
On June 7, 1776, Richard Henry Lee of Virginia, introduced this resolution in the Second Continental Congress
proposing independence for the American colonies
On June 11, 1776, the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution
one to draft a declaration of independence
On that date, Congress adopted the first part (the declaration).
New York cast no vote until the newly elected New York Convention upheld the Declaration of Independence on July 9, 1776.

events.label: New York upholds Declaration of Independence

evidence.quote: The plan for making treaties was not approved until September of 1776
the plan of confederation was delayed until November of 1777
